name: Jehozadak
overview: Jehozadak was a male Levite who served as an Aaronic priest through the line of Eleazar. He was the son of Seraiah and is noted for having gone into exile with the people of Judah under Nebuchadnezzar. His priestly heritage and participation in the exile highlight his role during a pivotal period in Israel's history.
namesAndTitles: The name Jehozadak means 'YHWH is just,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning tied to God's righteousness. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:14.
familyAndRelationships: Jehozadak is identified as the son of Seraiah, as noted in 1 Chronicles 6:14. Scripture does not record any additional family relationships beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Jehozadak's significance lies in his priestly lineage as an Aaronic priest descending through Eleazar, which underscores his role in maintaining the priesthood during a time of national crisis. His exile with Judah under Nebuchadnezzar marks him as part of the faithful remnant taken captive, representing continuity of the Levitical priesthood despite the Babylonian captivity.
